heading: Begin with a regional question
intro: Your first useful read depends on what you still need to decide. If the destination is open, compare the setting and journey before choosing a property. If you already have a base in mind, read its regional guide alongside the proposed outings. Keep a small shortlist so each new page helps answer a question rather than adding another place to an ever-longer itinerary.
points: Read one destination guide before expanding the shortlist.
Compare the proposed base and excursion settings.
Keep your own starting point in the comparison.

heading: Read the days behind the headline
intro: Trip length becomes clearer when you separate accommodation nights, transfer periods and full activities. Use the duration guides to frame that comparison, then return to the provider’s daily schedule. An extra day is useful when it supports something you value, whether more observation time or a gentler pace. The itinerary should explain where that time comes from.
points: Count nights and full activity periods separately.
Check the program for your actual dates.
Compare three-, four- and five-day structures.

heading: Look beyond the lodge photograph
intro: Accommodation research is more useful when a beautiful image leads to concrete questions. Review rooms, meals, guiding and excursions together, and ask which arrangements are confirmed for your group. Compare a written proposal with your comfort and mobility requirements. Keep assumptions out of the shortlist: a general regional description cannot establish the facilities of an individual property.
points: Request the room and meal arrangements.
Confirm requirements with the actual property.

heading: Follow your wildlife interests
intro: The animal and bird guides introduce regional examples and ways to think about observation. Read them for ideas, then ask about the habitat and interpretation of the actual outing. A photograph records a particular observation; it cannot be your future checklist. Give equal attention to the surroundings, the guide and the time available to notice what is there.
points: Ask about observations from the proposed area.
Confirm the guide’s experience and language.
Treat a target animal as an interest, not a promise.

heading: Connect access, timing and packing
intro: Use the access, timing and packing guides together. Start with the complete proposed route and dates, then ask what equipment the provider supplies and what you need to carry. Check onward plans before treating arrival or departure as a full activity day. Read the current official advice separately from general travel inspiration; gateways and transfers deserve attention too.
points: Ask for the complete transfer sequence.
Check the equipment list for the specific booking.
Review current official advice for each route.

heading: Turn reading into a focused inquiry
intro: When your shortlist is clear, move to the trip-planning guide. Share dates, group, starting point and a few priorities instead of sending every idea you have collected. Ask the provider to answer the unresolved questions in the proposal. Keep the final itinerary, inclusions and terms together so the reading supports a decision you understand.
points: Share a few priorities, dates and group details.
Save the final proposal and provider contacts.
